content.comment_body: Hello, I am using a [product_name] [article_no] (brand new). I updated the firmware with the latest version from the website ([version_no]). I'm currently working with [product_name] [version_no] software, previously using an older version and updated in hopes of resolving this issue. I am unable to download programs or access the [product_name] via the software (over Ethernet), as it always requests a password. I have cleared all passwords on the device and software, even though it was brand new and had no program. The software can connect to the device but cannot perform any operations. I also tried creating a new program by copying function blocks into a new file, and attempted to upload different programs, but neither worked. Another [product_name] (same model, possibly with older firmware) shows the same behavior. I am reluctant to clear its program, as I currently have no way to upload back to it. I’m considering loading the program via SD card and purchasing a new copy of the software (since I can’t find my original DVD) to attempt a reinstall. Any suggestions would be appreciated. Thanks

That is interesting. Recently, another user described a very similar issue in a topic here: [url] They also have the newest [product_name] with the latest firmware [version_no], but without a display. Edit: Is it possible you're experiencing conflicts with IP addresses? The password prompt might indicate an issue with the Ethernet connection. If the [product_name] responds too slowly, a password request can also appear.

Hi [user_name], Thanks for your input. I have initiated a support request, but your edit suggestion resolved the issue. All I needed to do was disable my Wi-Fi adapter. I didn't expect it to help since only the [product_name] was connected to the network card, but it immediately worked. Thanks again.
Was your Wi-Fi adapter enabled when you installed the [product_name] software?

No, I disabled it, connected and uploaded the software, then re-enabled the adapter. Edit: I assume you mean the program itself, not the firmware or [product_name] configuration software? Firmware was installed via microSD card, and the configuration software would have been installed with the adapter enabled.
No, I’m referring to the software, not the firmware. Is the problem resolved now?
Yes, the problem is resolved. I can now upload programs even with the Wi-Fi adapter enabled. Thank you for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered access and upload issues with a new [product_name] device as software repeatedly requested a password, despite no credentials being set. Investigation revealed that network interface conflicts, particularly with an active Wi-Fi adapter, disrupted Ethernet communication and triggered the password prompt, preventing operation. Disabling the Wi-Fi adapter resolved the problem, restoring expected functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable program upload/download without unnecessary password prompts or network conflicts, and straightforward operation on new, unused devices.
